name: grain-gradient
summary: Full-bleed hero running Paper Shaders' grain gradient on WebGL2: four colour stops pushed into the corners of a near-black field and broken up by a moving speckle, so the blend reads as printed grain rather than as a smooth ramp.

colors.description: Up to seven colour stops. Omit to read --fx-c1 through --fx-c4 off the section, which is what keeps the shader and the CSS resting state on one palette. Upstream default preset.

speed.description: Rate the colour field moves. 0 renders a single static frame. Forced to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion.

softness.description: How far each colour bleeds into its neighbour. 0 gives hard edges between the stops.

intensity.description: Size of the grain speckle that breaks the blend up.

noise.description: How much grain is mixed over the finished blend. 0 is a clean gradient.

deviations.what: The noise texture is decoded before ShaderMount is constructed, so the shader starts one microtask later than a React mount would.
deviations.why: Seam. Upstream's React component hands getShaderNoiseTexture() straight to ShaderMount and re-renders when it loads; a vanilla mount has no re-render, and ShaderMount throws on an image that is not complete. The image is a data: URI, so nothing is fetched.
